title: Local record — report row (D18)
description:
The shape of a report row. Durable capture is JSONL; SQLite is a rebuildable index, owned by tendcf-agent on Android and with ownership unresolved on Linux and macOS (guide §6 / map §8, D18 as amended by D45 on 2026-11-02). Nothing writes rows yet; the schema is settled now because it is schema — one column now and a migration later.

Two requirements from the Bcfg2 papers are load-bearing here:
  1. EVERY row carries the signed release that produced it, and the device records which release it is converged to (LISA '06 revision-stamping).
  2. Coverage is a COUNTER per domain, not just a list of discrepancies, and `not-yet-migrated` and `deliberately-unmanaged` are counted SEPARATELY. Conflating them is what makes the number stop meaning anything: one is backlog, the other is permanent by design.

The SQLite DDL is derived from this schema; this file is the contract, the DDL is a rendering of it.

release.description: The release that produced this row. Required on every row kind — this is what makes 'what was the desired state of device X at time T' reconstructible and 'did this break after the last release' a query rather than an argument.

promise_outcome.title: promise_outcome row
promise_outcome.description: One CFEngine promise outcome, ingested from the local JSONL capture. On Community that log needs a small piece of glue; the vocabulary is ncf's, kept verbatim.

entry.description: The promiser this outcome is about — a service name, a path, a package.

outcome.description: Vocabulary depends on `mode` — enforce and audit are different questions and must not share a value space.

blocked_by_interlock.description: Set when this entry was not modified because an interlock's pre-action failed (D16(c)). A blocked entry is not an error and must not be counted as one.

domain_coverage_row.title: domain_coverage row
domain_coverage_row.description: The managed/unmanaged ratio per domain, recorded as a quantity. This is what turns comprehensiveness from a lint into the build order's progress metric: Bcfg2's first client run reports 0 managed / 2308 unmanaged, and the whole deployment story is grinding that second number down. `extra_scan` says whether the extra-entry scan ran and finished: `complete` carries all three counters (extra_entries, two_writers, unmet_absence), defined for every supervisor's scan and zero where the detector has no such verdict, because a complete launchd row must carry them too; `incomplete` (the scan could not enumerate every in-scope unit with evidence) and `not-run` (the gate did not pass, or the domain is not scanned) carry none of them. An incomplete scan cannot carry a zero, because it cannot carry a count: a partial count is never reported as a total (schema v5, R3d).

managed.description: Entries described by the Site Model and under management.

not_yet_migrated.description: Backlog. Counted separately from deliberately-unmanaged BY DECISION — this is the number the build order drives to zero.

deliberately_unmanaged.description: Permanent by design and should be rare. Never added to not_yet_migrated.

extra_entries.description: Present on the device, absent from a comprehensive domain's description (D16(d) two-way verification). The multi-writer skew signal. Carried only on a `complete` scan (`extra_scan`): an incomplete or not-run scan has no count to give.

extra_scan.description: Whether the extra-entry scan of this domain ran to completion (schema v5, R3d). `complete`: every in-scope unit was resolved with evidence, and the three counters are present. `incomplete`: the gate passed but the scan could not finish (manager unreachable, dpkg database unusable, an unverifiable artifact, contradictory service declarations); no counter is carried. `not-run`: the gate did not pass (domain not comprehensive, or supervisor not systemd) or no detector exists for the domain; no counter is carried.

two_writers.description: Units shaped by a writer the goal file does not name for them: a claim and a vendor fragment on one name, a local fragment hiding a vendor one, or a local drop-in or mask on a vendor unit with no exact non-cfengine claim (schema v5 §3.4). Carried only on a `complete` scan; zero where the detector has no such verdict.

unmet_absence.description: A cfengine-claimed local fragment whose service entry is a tombstone: the removal the goal file asks for has not happened (schema v5 §3.4 row 6). Carried only on a `complete` scan; zero where the detector has no such verdict.

device_convergence.title: device_convergence row
device_convergence.description: Which release this device is currently converged to. Answers 'which devices were exposed, over what window, and when were they actually patched' — worth more on a fleet whose devices are routinely unreachable than it was in the paper's always-on cluster.

complete.description: False when convergence stopped early — an interlock blocked a bundle, or the run was interrupted. A device that is partially converged must not read as converged.

schema_ceiling.description: Highest goal-file schema_version this device's validator fully interprets. What the D44 render rule reads to decide which version to render this host's goal file at — an integer, not a string, so comparison is never lexicographic (goal-file-schema-reconciliation-2026-08-15.md §12, correcting E1 §5.6's claim that this column already existed; map §9.6). For a host that has never reported, the compiler renders at the version enrolled at that host's first-adoption ceremony, not this column. Required now rather than optional-then-required: nothing writes rows yet, so there is no legacy row to be lenient about.

validator_version.description: The version of this device's validator: tendcf-agent on Android, tendcf-validate on Linux and macOS (map D45, 2026-11-02). This is diagnostic metadata, not the identity of the report-writing process. schema_ceiling is the claim used by the render rule.
